```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

The paper's real-data task predicts an exporter's 2019 trade-outcome tensor
from 2018 trade and covariates. This vignette shows how to obtain the official
sources, prepare the analysis inputs, and refit RGD/RGN. Building it does not
download data or run the long experiment. The scripts are in the `SegreCP`
GitHub source checkout under `reproducibility/real_data/`; raw and processed
trade values are not distributed with the package.

The analysis uses 80 exporters, six covariates, a `25 x 21 x 8` response
tensor per exporter, CP rank three, and five common folds of 16 exporters.
The covariates summarize tariffs, logistics, partner GDP, distance,
trade-agreement scope, and world demand. The registered preprocessing uses
three-level agreement scope, square-root 2018 trade-value weights, and
untransformed tariffs. Feature standardization and response centering use
each training fold only.

The sample screen also used 2019 WITS tariff availability, excluding KOR and
MEX. The recorded analysis is therefore not a strictly 2018-information-only
prospective design; the screen did not use 2019 trade outcomes.

## Official sources

The download scripts specify the required years, indicators, and reporter
requests. The official sources are:

| Input | Pinned source route | Analysis use |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Trade values and quantities | [CEPII BACI HS17 V202601 archive](https://www.cepii.fr/DATA_DOWNLOAD/baci/data/BACI_HS17_V202601.zip) ([catalogue](https://www.cepii.fr/CEPII/en/bdd_modele/bdd_modele_item.asp?id=37)) | 2018 sample selection and exposure weights; 2019 outcomes |
| Bilateral covariates | [CEPII Gravity V202211 archive](https://www.cepii.fr/DATA_DOWNLOAD/gravity/data/Gravity_rds_V202211.zip) ([catalogue](https://www.cepii.fr/CEPII/en/bdd_modele/bdd_modele_item.asp?id=8)) | 2018 distance and agreement scope |
| GDP and population | [World Bank WDI API](https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/all/indicator/NY.GDP.MKTP.CD?date=2018:2019&format=json&per_page=20000) | 2018 market-size inputs |
| Logistics | [World Bank LPI API](https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/all/indicator/LP.LPI.OVRL.XQ?date=2018&format=json&per_page=20000) | 2018 logistics proxy |
| MFN tariffs | [WITS/UNCTAD TRAINS API](https://wits.worldbank.org/) | 2018 importer-by-section tariffs |

The WDI script also requests GDP per capita and population. The WITS script
uses official availability information to choose each reporter's tariff
schedule. The CEPII Gravity archive contains the `Gravity_V202211.rds` file
used by the analysis. Versions and API responses may change; preparation
checks the downloaded data against the recorded sources before using them.
Follow each provider's access terms, particularly the
[UNCTAD TRAINS terms](https://wits.worldbank.org/data/public/UNCTAD_TermsofUseandDisclaimer.pdf),
which restrict redistribution without written permission.

## Rebuild and check the inputs

Run the following commands from the `SegreCP` source checkout. They are shown
for readers, not executed while building this vignette. You need R >= 4.2, a
C++ build toolchain, and the R packages listed below. Online preparation also
uses `bash`, `curl`, and `unzip`. Choose a private absolute path outside the
checkout on a Unix-like system and allow several gigabytes of disk space.

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
# From the SegreCP source directory; edit this private path first.
TRADE_DATA_DIR=/absolute/path/to/private-trade-work
Rscript -e 'install.packages(c("Rcpp", "rTensor", "data.table", "digest", "jsonlite", "xml2"), repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")'
R CMD INSTALL .
Rscript reproducibility/real_data/run.R \
  --prepare --data-dir="$TRADE_DATA_DIR"
Rscript reproducibility/real_data/run.R \
  --check-inputs --data-dir="$TRADE_DATA_DIR"
```

If the official source files are already present under the private directory
at the paths listed in the source manifest, use `--prepare --offline` instead.
If a provider no longer serves the recorded version, obtain that version
through the provider's official route before using offline preparation.
Preparation does not overwrite existing analysis inputs unless
`--overwrite-derived` is explicitly requested; a new private directory is
best for an independent run.

The four prepared inputs are:

| Input | Meaning |
|:--|:--|
| Response tensor | Exporter keys and 2019 outcomes |
| Design matrix | Six 2018 exporter-level features |
| Fold assignments | Five balanced exporter folds |
| Preprocessing registry | Registered transformations and feature order |

`run.R --check-inputs` verifies the recorded source version and the prepared
inputs, including their dimensions, keys, feature order, and folds. If only
the four processed files remain, `run.R --check-derived` verifies those
inputs alone. An offline rebuild from the recorded official files reproduced
the prepared analysis inputs. New provider downloads may differ, especially
for the live WITS API.

## Run the authors' package methods

The source-checkout script `fit_authors_methods.R` fits rank-three RGD and RGN
through `SegreCP::segre_regress()`. It uses the common folds and estimates
feature scaling and response centering from each training fold. Its
`--check-inputs` option checks the four prepared inputs; the full command
runs five folds and five timing repetitions. Both write outside the package.

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
# From the SegreCP source directory, with SegreCP installed and the four
# processed files already checked. Edit this path if using a new shell.
TRADE_DATA_DIR=/absolute/path/to/private-trade-work
Rscript reproducibility/real_data/fit_authors_methods.R \
  --check-inputs --data-dir="$TRADE_DATA_DIR"
Rscript reproducibility/real_data/fit_authors_methods.R \
  --smoke --data-dir="$TRADE_DATA_DIR" \
  --output-dir="$TRADE_DATA_DIR/authors-smoke"
Rscript reproducibility/real_data/fit_authors_methods.R \
  --folds=1,2,3,4,5 --repetitions=5 --data-dir="$TRADE_DATA_DIR" \
  --output-dir="$TRADE_DATA_DIR/authors-results"
```

The full run writes `authors_methods_per_fold.csv`,
`authors_methods_summary.csv`, and `authors_methods_objective.csv` to the
chosen output directory; smoke files use the `authors_methods_smoke_`
prefix. A local full run matched the recorded RGD/RGN accuracy rows to
numerical precision, with mean test RMSE 2.7003 for RGD and 2.6684 for RGN.
The smoke run is only a quick execution check. Elapsed times depend on the
machine.

To visualize empirical convergence after the full run, plot the observed
training objective from the private result file.

```{r real-objective-plot, eval=FALSE}
result_dir <- "/absolute/path/to/private-trade-work/authors-results"
trace <- read.csv(file.path(result_dir, "authors_methods_objective.csv"))
trace <- subset(trace, fold == 1L & repetition == 1L)
rgd <- subset(trace, method == "RGD")
rgn <- subset(trace, method == "RGN")
stopifnot(nrow(rgd) > 0L, nrow(rgn) > 0L,
          all(rgd$objective_ratio > 0), all(rgn$objective_ratio > 0))
plot(rgd$iteration, rgd$objective_ratio, type = "b", log = "y",
     xlab = "Completed sweep", ylab = "Training objective / initial objective",
     col = "#1f77b4", pch = 16)
lines(rgn$iteration, rgn$objective_ratio, type = "b",
      col = "#d95f02", pch = 17)
legend("topright", c("RGD", "RGN"), col = c("#1f77b4", "#d95f02"),
       pch = c(16, 17), lty = 1, bty = "n")
```

## Work with one prepared fold

The following example shows the transformations and one RGN fit for a single
fold. Run it from the source checkout after preparing the private data. It is
not the five-fold paper protocol and is not evaluated during package checks.

```{r real-fold, eval=FALSE}
source("reproducibility/real_data/read_prepared_trade_data.R")
trade_data_dir <- "/absolute/path/to/private-trade-work"
trade <- read_prepared_trade_data(trade_data_dir)
X <- trade$X
Y <- trade$Y
fold <- trade$fold
train <- which(fold != 1L)
test <- which(fold == 1L)
x_mean <- colMeans(X[train, , drop = FALSE])
x_sd <- pmax(apply(X[train, , drop = FALSE], 2L, sd), 1e-12)
X_train <- sweep(sweep(X[train, , drop = FALSE], 2L, x_mean),
                 2L, x_sd, "/")
X_test <- sweep(sweep(X[test, , drop = FALSE], 2L, x_mean),
                2L, x_sd, "/")

y_mean <- apply(Y[train, , , , drop = FALSE], 4L, mean)
Y_train <- sweep(Y[train, , , , drop = FALSE], 4L, y_mean)
Y_test <- sweep(Y[test, , , , drop = FALSE], 4L, y_mean)

fit <- SegreCP::segre_regress(
  X_train, Y_train, rank = 3L,
  input_dims = 6L, output_dims = c(25L, 21L, 8L),
  method = "rgn", init = "cpca", init_split = c(1L, 2L),
  design_variance = 1,
  control = SegreCP::segre_control(
    profile = "practical", max_iter = 30L, tolerance = 0,
    step_size = 0.5, step_rule = "backtracking",
    component_order = "decreasing_weight", ridge = 1e-6,
    normalize_regression = "none"
  )
)
prediction <- predict(fit, X_test)
sqrt(mean((as.numeric(prediction) - as.numeric(Y_test))^2))
```

The saved seven-method comparison uses a separate benchmark. This checkout
provides fresh RGD/RGN fits for the trade analysis; its synthetic simulation
results appear in the other numerical-results vignettes.

## Minimal installed-package example

This small synthetic example runs during vignette building to check the
tensor-on-tensor input convention without downloading any trade data.

```{r small-api-example}
set.seed(41)
X_demo <- matrix(rnorm(30L * 6L), nrow = 30L)
factors <- lapply(c(6L, 3L, 2L), function(p) {
  z <- rnorm(p)
  z / sqrt(sum(z^2))
})
beta <- array(2 * Reduce(kronecker, rev(factors)), dim = c(6L, 3L, 2L))
Y_demo <- array(as.numeric(X_demo %*% matrix(beta, nrow = 6L)),
                dim = c(30L, 3L, 2L))

demo_fit <- SegreCP::segre_regress(
  X_demo, Y_demo, rank = 1L,
  input_dims = 6L, output_dims = c(3L, 2L),
  method = "rgn", init = "hosvd",
  control = SegreCP::segre_control(max_iter = 2L)
)
dim(predict(demo_fit, X_demo[1:2, , drop = FALSE]))
```
